title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
reason: As someone with a molecular biology background navigating a career change and migration, Harari's sweeping synthesis of human history speaks directly to my current existential questions. The book bridges hard science and humanistic inquiry — precisely the kind of cross-disciplinary thinking I find valuable right now. At £54.23 it is not cheap, but for a title I would genuinely read rather than shelve, it is worth the spend. The five-star rating on the catalog does not hurt either, even if the site warns that ratings are random.
